program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

fulfillment: The binding is too broad and the node treats the final spatial relation as sufficient proof of the requested edit. In the edited image, a mug is indeed to the right of the headphones, but the source shows the mug to their left; the edit appears to add/move a mug to the right while leaving a mug-like object on the left, so the requested change has progressed without clearly being completed. Make the criterion compare the same target mug’s position in the source and edited snapshots, and distinguish partial progress from completion when the requested relocation is not unambiguously complete. Do not infer completion from two support observations that repeat the same final-state claim; they are dependent on the same evidence, not independent confirmation. Preserve unknown for genuinely insufficient evidence, and keep transport/schema failures separate from visual evidence—none are reported here.
s2: The binding checks only whether a mug is right of the headphones in the edited snapshot, so it mistakes a final-state relation for completion of the requested relocation. Make the node track the same source mug across snapshots and assess its displacement relative to the headphones; distinguish a completed move from partial progress when the original mug remains or the target’s identity/continuity is ambiguous. Here the source mug is left of the headphones, while the edited image appears to retain a mug on the left and show another on the right, supporting progress but not clearly proving the original mug was moved. Avoid treating the dependent s1/s2 observations as independent confirmation. Keep unknown for genuinely unresolved identity or visibility, and do not conflate visual uncertainty with transport/schema failure (none is reported).
s1: The node’s current binding only checks whether a mug and headphones can be compared in the edited image; that is an evidence-availability check, not a fulfillment judgment. Keep that distinction explicit, and ensure downstream fulfillment compares the source and edited snapshots, tracking the original mug rather than treating any mug to the headphones’ right as proof of completion. Here, the source has one blue mug left of the headphones; the edited image shows a blurred blue shape on the left and two smaller mugs, one on each side of the headphones. This supports some change, but does not clearly establish that the original mug was relocated to the right. Preserve unresolved when identity or continuity cannot be judged; do not turn uncertainty into a negative visual finding. The single high-confidence pass establishes visibility only, and repeated dependent observations would not be independent confirmation. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported.

findings.source_phrase: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
findings.question: Does the edited image show the original mug moved to the right of the headphones, rather than merely showing a mug in that position while the original mug remains elsewhere?
findings.criteria: Compare source and edited images to track the mug and headphones. Pass only if the mug from the source is now to the headphones’ right; fail if the source mug remains in its original left-side position and the right-side mug is an additional object; unknown if object continuity cannot be judged.
findings.evidence: The source shows one large blue mug left of the headphones. The edited image appears to show a blue blurred shape at the left, a small mug left of the headphones, and another mug to their right. The saved checks only assert that a visible mug is right of the headphones.
findings.rationale: The broad relative-position check can pass without establishing that the requested mug was moved. The edited image raises a concrete identity/continuity question, so the saved pass and fulfillment readout may overclaim completion. A focused source-to-edit comparison is needed; it should not assume the blur is definitively the original mug.
